slides.text: November isn't the end of the season here. <hl>It's a planting month.</hl>

slides.heading: Garlic Goes In <hl>Now</hl>
slides.body: Break a head into cloves and plant each one pointy end up, a couple of inches deep, in a sunny spot. In our area the window runs fall through early winter. One clove becomes one head next summer.

slides.heading: Peas and <hl>Fava Beans</hl>
slides.body: Both love our cool, damp winters. Sow seeds straight into the soil and give peas something to climb — a stick and some string is plenty. Favas feed your soil while they grow.

slides.heading: Greens That Don't <hl>Mind the Cold</hl>
items: Bok choy and other Asian greens
All happy in a bed, a pot or a balcony planter

slides.heading: Rain's Coming — <hl>Ease Off the Hose</hl>
slides.body: Once the rains start, most gardens in our area need far less watering. Check the soil with a finger before you water, and mulch your beds to hold moisture.

slides.heading: Not Sure What Fits <hl>Your Space?</hl>
slides.body: That's what our free, in-person class is for — soil, water, sunlight, and what to plant when, taught by Jason every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda. You leave with a plan for your own yard, balcony or raised bed.

caption.instagram:
November isn't the end of the season here in Alameda — it's a planting month. 🌱

Garlic, peas, fava beans, lettuce, kale and chard all go in now in our area, and once the rains start you can ease off the hose. Not sure what fits your space? That's exactly what our free, in-person class is for, taught by Jason every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda.
